summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — HOOD +10%, XYZ +7%, TTWO +6%, GEV +6%, VRT +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CBOE -9%, MPWR -9%, SATS -7%, APP -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HOOD (+10.34%) — Argus raised HOOD price target from $90 to $110 (Buy); company also announced ~10% workforce cut (290 roles) on Jun 16 to flatten org layers — market re-rated on margin improvement thesis. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — HOOD is a mid-cap fintech brokerage excluded by current sector filters. The move was analyst-upgrade-driven; post-open momentum signals arrived well after the gap was already priced in.

top_movers.catalyst: Argus raised HOOD price target from $90 to $110 (Buy); company also announced ~10% workforce cut (290 roles) on Jun 16 to flatten org layers — market re-rated on margin improvement thesis.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HOOD is a mid-cap fintech brokerage excluded by current sector filters. The move was analyst-upgrade-driven; post-open momentum signals arrived well after the gap was already priced in.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-upgrade event gate: when a tier-1 firm raises a fintech name's price target by ≥15% above prior close pre-market, admit it to the news-reactive strategy universe at open with a half-size cap.

top_movers.catalyst: ARK Investment disclosed a 237K-share Block (XYZ) purchase on June 17; move amplified by backdrop of Q1 EPS beat ($0.85 vs $0.60 est, +42%) and Goldman Sachs Conviction List addition.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (fintech/payments, NYSE). The +6.95% move was triggered by ARK's 237K-share buy disclosure — a catalyst requiring real-time institutional-filing feeds, not capturable by price/volume signals alone.
top_movers.suggestion: Subscribe to ARK's daily holdings feed; admit any name with ≥100K new ARK shares and a confirmed ≥3% gap at open into the momentum strategy's universe for that session only.

top_movers.catalyst: Rockstar Games revealed GTA VI pre-order start date of June 25, 2026, reigniting hype ahead of the confirmed Nov 19 release; analysts project 45M+ launch units driving FY2027 net bookings of $8B+.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TTWO (~$42B cap, Communication Services/Interactive Media) trades on product-cycle narrative; the +6% move was triggered by a pre-order announcement — a one-off event-driven catalyst that requires pre-market news scanning, not technical signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gaming-event watchlist (TTWO, EA, ATVI-class) to the news-reactive strategy's universe, gated on a 'product-milestone' keyword filter (pre-order|release-date|launch), with a 30-min open momentum entry and hard 2% stop.

top_movers.catalyst: GEV released 2025 Sustainability Report (26 GW deployed, nuclear/SMR progress) June 18; update reinforced the AI data-center power thesis in a sector-wide bid for grid-infrastructure names.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. GEV is an industrials/capital-goods name (~$1,000/share) excluded from energy/utilities sector filters. Its 15% ATH pullback ($1,149→$982) would also fail momentum minimum-trend screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Create a power-infrastructure overlay universe covering industrial capital-goods names (backlog growth ≥25% YoY, order intake rising) with a news-catalyst trigger gate in lieu of price-momentum filters to capture GEV-style moves.

top_movers.catalyst: Bernstein issued a bullish upgrade calling VRT 'highly attractive after recent pullback'; Vertiv also confirmed completion of the ThermoKey (AI data-center heat-exchange) acquisition — combined analyst + M&A catalyst fuelled a two-day momentum surge.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. VRT is a large-cap AI-infrastructure industrial (~$100B+ market cap); the bot's universe likely excludes this sector/cap tier. The two-day analyst+M&A rally also required pre-positioning before post-open signals could register.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an AI data-center infrastructure sub-universe (VRT, ETN, SMCI-class names, mcap >$20B) to the news-reactive strategy, gated on same-day analyst-upgrade filings or 8-K M&A completions with open gap ≥+3%.

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised WDC price target 33% to $650 (from $488) citing AI-driven HDD shortage persisting through 2028; JPMorgan, Mizuho, and Citi also lifted targets, extending a multi-day analyst-upgrade rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. WDC is up ~282% YTD and printing all-time highs ~$723, which places it above typical RSI/distance-from-52w-high admission thresholds. The triggering Morgan Stanley note dropped Sunday June 15, requiring pre-weekend positioning the bot cannot take.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-upgrade event scanner: when ≥2 brokers raise price targets ≥20% on the same name within 48 hours, admit it to the momentum universe for up to 3 sessions with a max-position cap of 0.5× normal size, gated on confirmed gap-continuation (open ≥+2% vs. prior close).

top_movers.catalyst: CME Group sued the CFTC on June 18 over its perpetual-futures approval, escalating multi-session competition fears for incumbent exchanges and extending CBOE's 3-day ~18% sector re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CBOE is a large-cap exchange operator caught in a regulatory/competitive re-rating that built over three sessions; single-session momentum and news-gap filters cannot catch a structural sell-off seeded by a headline from June 2.
top_movers.suggestion: Add exchange-sector names (CBOE, CME, ICE) to a regulatory-event short watchlist: trigger entry when cumulative 3-session loss ≥8% follows a CFTC/SEC competitive-threat headline, short at next open with a 5% hard stop — requires short capability.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued sector-wide semiconductor repricing from Broadcom's soft AI forward guidance (June 3), compounding MPWR's premium valuation overhang (NTM EV/EBITDA ~49x vs peer median ~21x) and an unresolved Feb-2026 audit-committee accounting restatement.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MPWR is a large-cap (~$70B) high-multiple semiconductor name; its valuation extreme (49x EV/EBITDA) and open restatement likely place it outside quality or value screens, and the decline was sector-sentiment-driven rather than a discrete tradeable catalyst signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-beta short proxy rule: when SOXX drops ≥3% intraday, a pairs or index-short leg should activate for overvalued semis (NTM EV/EBITDA ≥2× peer median) — this would capture MPWR-analogue moves without requiring individual name universe expansion.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-SpaceX-IPO (SPCX) rotation: investors sold EchoStar's indirect ~2% SpaceX stake (via spectrum deal) to buy SPCX directly after its June 12 debut; a deferred $183M DISH DBS interest payment nearing its 30-day default deadline added further selling pressure.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. EchoStar is a holding-company SpaceX proxy whose price action tracks SPCX sentiment; the drop was an IPO-rotation unwind — not foreseeable from technical signals — in a name up 543% over 12 months with active debt-default risk.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'proxy-unwind' trigger: when a newly listed name (e.g., SPCX) debuts and correlates ≥0.7 intraday with a universe candidate, flag that candidate as a short within 5 sessions of IPO open; if short capability is absent, mark it as a forced exclude to avoid erroneous long entries.

top_movers.catalyst: CEO Foroughi sold $25M+ in Class A shares (Form 4 filings, mid-June) amid an active SEC consumer-data investigation and mounting pre-launch execution anxiety over AXON ad platform's global self-serve rollout in late June 2026.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. APP is a large-cap ad-tech stock whose 3-session slide (-4.4%, -3.3%, -6.1%) required short capability and prior coverage — not a single-session news-reactive entry the bot's filters could fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — catching this as a short requires adding large-cap ad-tech names to the universe and enabling short capability; without both prerequisites, adding APP only exposes the bot to the long side of an ongoing downtrend.
